company_name: Zhou Liu Fu Jewellery Co., Ltd.

inputs.share_count_basis: 440,616,028 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (166,927,145 unlisted + 273,688,883 H) less 13,220,300 H shares held in treasury = 427.396m. Interim note 9: no potentially dilutive ordinary shares. A further 329,700 H shares were repurchased in July 2026 (not deducted; immaterial). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated statement of changes in equity, share-based payments RMB6,142k (Annual_FY2025.txt:9821); no equity-award taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in kpis). Equity-settled RSUs granted at RMB2.08 to 52 employees are immaterial.
inputs.buyback_note: H1 FY2026 only: 13,220,300 H shares repurchased for HKD222.65m (RMB194.1m), held as treasury shares. FY2025 and earlier: nil. The flat count is being funded by a live repurchase programme (mandate up to 27.28m shares, May 2026).
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1747, Yahoo Finance CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-23. Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. Per-share values computed in CNY then multiplied by 1.1747. No dual listing exists for a parity check (H-share only; unlisted domestic shares); magnitude check: FY2025 EPS RMB1.88 x 1.1747 = HK$2.21 against a HK$10.76 price gives P/E 4.9x, consistent with the ~5-7x screen P/E.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10y China Government Bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~7%, beta ~1.2 for a small-cap HK-listed Chinese discretionary retailer with a 16-month listing history -> cost of equity ~10.2%; debt is ~13% of capital at ~2.5% pre-tax, so WACC rounds to 10.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, VAT reform, franchise contraction and governance risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease cash = principal RMB30.558m (financing, Annual_FY2025.txt:9987) + interest RMB1.726m (:12630) = RMB32.3m = 0.55% of revenue; H1 FY2026 RMB15.8m = 0.67%. Charged via lease_cost_pct_path (0.6% base). Lease liabilities (RMB25.2m at 30 June 2026) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 D&A RMB83.6m less ROU depreciation RMB32.4m (:9913) = RMB51.3m = 0.88% of revenue.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI stock of RMB16.243m at 30 June 2026 deducted once in equity_bridge. NCI share of profit was RMB9.9m in H1 FY2026 (new overseas JV stores) -- small enough that an attributable-flow leakage driver is not warranted.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon (FY2026-FY2035), scenario-weighted -- Zhou Liu Fu is an operating jewellery retailer/franchisor, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (non-US, cyclical consumer) with the adaptations file applied: CNY WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI in bridge, FVTPL financial assets in bridge, CNY/HKD fx bridge. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). last_fcf = reported_fcf -166.731 - SBC 6.142 - interest income 23.881 = -196.754 (FY2025 owner FCF); net cash was RMB743m at 31 Dec 2025 (> FCF base) so interest income is stripped from the history for a consistent owner-FCF series. Net cash has since fallen to RMB49m at 30 June 2026 and no interest income is in the forward component build. FY2025 owner FCF is negative because of an RMB896m inventory build (gold-price revaluation of stock plus Miaoji gold-bar inventory) on only +2% revenue; H1 FY2026 added a further RMB398m build on -25% revenue. The forward build does NOT extrapolate negative FCF: it is a component build from EBITDA (18.0% FY2025, 22.7% H1 FY2026) with capex normalising after the Shenzhen HQ construction (RMB198m in H1 FY2026, RMB135.7m commitments outstanding) and a modest working-capital charge on revenue change. KNOWN LIMITATION: wc_capture x delta-revenue cannot represent gold-price-driven inventory revaluation; base -15% capture on a -20% FY2026 revenue year implies a ~RMB175m working-capital RELEASE in FY2026, whereas H1 FY2026 actually consumed RMB398m. The first-year FCF is therefore optimistic by roughly RMB0.5-1.0/share if gold keeps inflating the carrying value of stock; the bear case sets capture to 0 to represent no destocking release. Share-count basis: fully issued less treasury, flat. Price is the 2026-10-23 regular close (not after-hours). Tax: preferential 15% rates on key subsidiaries run to 2030 (effective ~19.4% FY2025, 20.2% FY2024, statutory 25%); cash tax path holds 20% to FY2030 then steps to 22-23%.

equity_bridge.item: Financial assets at FVTPL (wealth-management products) at carrying value, 30 June 2026
equity_bridge.note: HalfYear_H1-2026 statement of financial position; not in cash and bank balances, no income from them is in the flows
Overseas JV stores; charged once here, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case FY2027 recovery growth. Equity CAGR is inflated by the June 2025 IPO proceeds (~RMB1.15bn) and revenue CAGR by the FY2022-24 franchise store roll-out that has since reversed (franchise stores 4,038 -> 3,209); neither is a forward proxy.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 30.7% vs EPS 3yr CAGR 6.2% and revenue 23.4%: the equity series is distorted by the IPO raise, not by retained earnings. H1 FY2026 revenue -25% YoY breaks the trend entirely.
historical_growth.notes: Only FY2022-FY2025 revenue/EPS/equity exist (FY2022-23 from the annual report's summary table); cash-flow data start FY2024. Owner FCF: FY2024 RMB53.6m (65.9 - 4.9 SBC - 7.4 interest), FY2025 RMB-196.8m -- a CAGR is not computable on a sign change. Reported FCF went from +65.9 to -166.7; the owner-FCF series is lower by the SBC and interest-income strip in both years. Weighted-average shares rose with the IPO so EPS understates attributable profit growth (+9% FY2025).

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue -20% (H1 -25%, H2 easing as franchise destocking abates and online regains growth per the interim outlook); recovery to mid-single-digit growth FY2027-30 as self-operated and online growth outweighs a smaller franchise base; fades to 2.5% terminal. EBITDA margin 21% FY2026 (H1 22.7% on gold-price gross margin) settling at 20%, above the 18% FY2025 level because the mix is shifting to online, self-operated and fixed-price 'cultural premium' product. Capex 7.5% in FY2026 while the HQ completes, then 1.5% maintenance. Working capital consumes 15c per RMB of revenue growth. Cap multiple 12x FCF for a cyclical discretionary retailer; Gordon at 10%/2.5% would be 13.7x so the cap binds.

bull.narrative: Gold price stabilises in H2 FY2026, franchise destocking ends and online (Miaoji gold bars, content platforms) resumes ~40%-style growth off a reset base: FY2026 -16%, then two years of 10% and a slow fade. Fixed-price and Jianbao heritage product lift gross margin structurally, EBITDA margin reaches 23%. Self-operated expansion (117 stores, Hainan duty-free, SE Asia) needs more capex (2%) and faster growth consumes more working capital (-25% capture).

bear.narrative: The Nov-2025 VAT reform (6% vs 13% input-VAT offset for non-exchange members) plus a continued shift from jewellery to investment bars keeps per-gram demand falling through 2027: FY2026 -28%, FY2027 -8%, FY2028 -3%, then ~2% nominal. Franchise network keeps shrinking and the gold-price gross-margin windfall reverses as prices fall: EBITDA margin fades to 15% (below FY2024's 16.8%). Working-capital capture set to 0: the revenue decline releases no cash because gold-price revaluation and gold-bar stock keep inventory elevated, as in H1 FY2026.

scenario_narratives.base: Cyclical trough in FY2026 with a moderate recovery. Online stays >50% of revenue and grows mid-to-high single digits, self-operated stores add ~5-10 a year, the franchise channel stabilises at ~3,000 quality-upgraded stores. Margin holds near 20% on mix; capex normalises once the HQ is finished; the buyback keeps the count flat. Value is ~48% terminal at a 12x FCF cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold stabilises, destocking ends, and Zhou Liu Fu's e-commerce execution reasserts itself with Miaoji and content-platform growth; cultural-premium product takes the EBITDA margin to 23%; overseas expansion adds a second leg. The stock re-rates from ~5x to a double-digit P/E.
scenario_narratives.bear: VAT reform, gold volatility and the jewellery-to-bars substitution make the FY2026 decline structural rather than cyclical; franchise revenue keeps shrinking, the gold-price margin windfall reverses, and inventory never converts to cash. The company stays GAAP-profitable but with FCF conversion well below earnings; the market's ~5x P/E proves roughly right.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: two consecutive periods of negative owner FCF from inventory, a live regulatory headwind (VAT reform through 2027), a franchise channel in net contraction, a 16-month listing record with an 80% drawdown from the 52-week high, and a non-core Going Securities investment (since exited at cost) that questions capital allocation. Bull cut to 20% because it needs gold stabilisation, franchise recovery AND an online re-acceleration together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on CNY flows at a 10% CNY WACC, converted to HKD at 1.1747. Reported FCF is negative on inventory build and is not extrapolated; the forward build is from components (EBITDA, lease, D&A ex-ROU, cash tax, normalised capex, working capital on revenue change). SBC is negligible (0.1% of revenue) so the house/street band is nearly a point. Terminal value is capped at 12x FCF, a multiple appropriate to a gold-price-exposed Chinese discretionary retailer, and binds in every scenario at 10% WACC. The gap between the model and the ~5x P/E market price is mostly a judgment about whether inventory ever converts to cash and whether the FY2026 decline is cyclical; both are carried in the 30% bear weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: Inventory conversion: NWC is ~65% of TTM revenue (inventory RMB3.54bn at 30 June 2026); if gold keeps inflating carrying values, FCF stays below earnings and the model's wc_capture on revenue change understates the cash drag (see inputs.notes)
FY2026 revenue trajectory: H1 was -25% and management guidance is qualitative and conditional on gold-price stabilisation in Q3
China gold VAT reform (effective 1 Nov 2025, to 2027) raising costs for non-exchange-member supply chains
Gross-margin durability: the 8.4pp H1 FY2026 gross-margin gain is partly a gold-price effect that reverses if prices fall
Franchise channel contraction (3,209 stores from 4,038 in 18 months) and franchisee credit/destocking behaviour
Governance and capital allocation as a newly listed H-share issuer (Going Securities investment, Sep 2025; exited Jul 2026 at cost)
CNY/HKD rate: refresh_price.py moves the price but not fx_rate; the 1.1747 bridge must be refreshed with the price
